text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

A panel's composition isn't evidence of bias on its own — selection panels are often skewed by whoever is available, and all-male panels pick men constantly without that being proof of anything either. Raising it as your opening argument makes you look like you're explaining away a loss, and it will harden attitudes against you.

Also, your case is weaker than it feels. For a group-head role, client relationships and leadership are often weighted above raw design years; 8 years plus chartership plus commercial strength is a plausible winner.

What *is* legitimate: chase the written explanation, in writing, citing their own process. Silence after two weeks is the real issue. Judge the decision once you see their reasons.
